findings_addressed.oracle: CR_NO_SUCH_DEVNODE (0x0000000D) is the Windows API return code documented in cfgmgr32.h for CM_Locate_DevNodeW when the device instance ID does not exist. It is an independent constant from the Windows SDK, not derived from any value the test injects. The bogus PnP ID "PCI\VEN_FFFF&DEV_FFFF&SUBSYS_FFFFFFFF&REV_FF\NOSUCHNODE" is guaranteed never to be present, so the real DLL must return 0x0000000D to pass.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/providers/gpu_pci_resources.py line 96, change `self.locate_devnode = self._lib.CM_Locate_DevNodeW` to `self.locate_devnode = self._lib.CM_Get_First_Log_Conf` — the misbound function has a different calling convention and would return a non-zero value that does not equal CR_NO_SUCH_DEVNODE, making the assertion fail.

findings_addressed.oracle: Every functional PCI GPU must have at least one non-zero MMIO memory BAR to be addressable by the OS. The minimum threshold of 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes) is physically motivated — no GPU allocates fewer than 1 MiB of MMIO address space. This is an independent physical constant, not derived from any value the test injects. Additionally, max_memory_bar_bytes() is cross-checked against an independent recomputation max(b.size_bytes for b in bars) to confirm both code paths agree on the same non-zero value.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/providers/gpu_pci_resources.py, change the nbytes_le slice in _parse_mem_descriptor from data[range_offset + 8 : range_offset + 16] / data[range_offset + 8 : range_offset + 12] to data[range_offset + 0 : range_offset + 8] / data[range_offset + 0 : range_offset + 4]. The first eight bytes of the MEM_DES header encode the base address (physical MMIO start), not the byte count. For most real GPU allocations those bytes would decode to 0 (if the base is stored elsewhere) or to a physical address value that does not equal the true BAR size. The min_gpu_bar_bytes assertion (size >= 1 MiB) would then fail because the wrong offset decodes to 0 or to an address rather than the true allocation length.

findings_addressed.oracle: buf[40:44] = 0x12345678 (little-endian, 4 bytes); buf[44:48] = 0x9ABCDEF0 (little-endian, 4 bytes, non-zero). Oracle: int.from_bytes(b'\x78\x56\x34\x12', 'little') == 305419896 == 0x12345678. A correct 4-byte read of data[40:44] returns 305419896. A wrong-width 8-byte read of data[40:48] returns 0x9ABCDEF012345678 == 11150879468389683832, which != oracle. The test asserts bar.size_bytes == oracle_32 AND bar.size_bytes != oracle_8byte_wrong, so the wrong-width mutation fails. The 0x12345678 value (305419896 bytes) is below any 32-bit overflow so no validation branch is tripped.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/providers/gpu_pci_resources.py _parse_mem_descriptor, change `data[range_offset + 8 : range_offset + 12]` (small path, 4 bytes) to `data[range_offset + 8 : range_offset + 16]` (8 bytes). With buf[44:48] = 0x9ABCDEF0, the 8-byte read decodes to 0x9ABCDEF012345678 != 0x12345678, causing the oracle assertion to fail.

notes: test_small_descriptor_decodes_uint32_size hardened: non-zero upper bytes at buf[44:48]=0x9ABCDEF0 make 4-byte vs 8-byte reads disagree; independent oracle computed via int.from_bytes over the injected bytes (oracle_32=0x12345678=305419896); test asserts size_bytes==oracle_32 AND size_bytes!=oracle_8byte_wrong. G0282 (test_loads_real_cfgmgr_on_windows) unchanged — already a strong gate asserting CR_NO_SUCH_DEVNODE.
